question.prompt:
In the figure below, the outside square contains infinitely many squares, each of them with the same center and sides parallel to the outside square. The ratio of the side length of each inner square to that of the next outer square is \(k,\) where \(0 \lt k \lt 1.\) The spaces between squares are alternately shaded, as shown in the figure (which is not necessarily drawn to scale).

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12A_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

The area of the shaded portion of the figure is \(64\%\) of the area of the original square. What is \(k?\)

solutions.explanation:
[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12A_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

The outermost frame is shaded, and the frames alternate in color. Because only an area percentage matters, choose area units in which the outside square has area \(100\). The shaded area is then \(64\), and the unshaded area is \(36\).

Shrink the entire arrangement toward its common center by the length factor \(k\). Every square moves to the next inner square. Consequently, each shaded frame moves to the following unshaded frame, and every unshaded frame is obtained exactly once this way. Since \(0<k<1\), the nested squares shrink to their common center, which contributes no area.

Multiplying side lengths by \(k\) multiplies square areas, and therefore frame areas, by \(k^2\). The correspondence between the shaded and unshaded frames gives
\[
36=64k^2,
\qquad k^2=\frac{9}{16}.
\]
The condition \(0<k<1\) selects the positive square root, so \(\boxed{k=\frac34}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the shaded and unshaded regions
